AIPAC spent $32 million through its main super PAC, the United Democracy Project, in an unsuccessful effort to defeat Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, a vocal critic of Israel and AIPAC, in Michigan’s Democratic Senate Primary. This month, which the super PAC entered with $59 million in its account, it took the extraordinary step of making plans to spend on behalf of Mr. Rogers, who has long been supportive of Israel, and against Dr. El-Sayed.

headline: Air Force Maj. Jason Watson has been formally charged under the Uniform Code of Military Justice following a series of public statements criticizing President Donald Trump, in and out of uniform. Watson faces three Article 88 charges alleging contemptuous remarks about the president, five Article 92 charges alleging violations of orders and regulations, and two Article 133 charges alleging conduct unbecoming an officer. The allegations relate to a June interview, his July 1 appearance at the U.S. Capitol while in uniform in support of Trump's impeachment, and an August 17 CNN interview. The Article 92 allegations also include alleged violations involving political activity, uniform wear, leave and an order to wear his uniform which he reportedly refused. Article 88 prosecutions are uncommon. A review cited by CNN identified only two convictions since the UCMJ was established in 1951, including the 2021 case of former Marine Lt. Col. Stuart Scheller, who criticized the Biden administration's handling of the Afghanistan withdrawal. Watson remains presumed innocent. The case will undergo the military justice process, including a potential Article 32 preliminary hearing, after which authorities will determine whether it proceeds to a special or general court-martial.

headline: The U.S. Army’s AH-64 'Apache' fleet is experiencing an unusually high rate of serious accidents, with five Class A mishaps so far in FY2026. A CNN analysis puts the current rate at roughly 6.24 Class A crashes per 100,000 flight hours, approaching the Army’s recent worst year of 2024, when the fleet recorded nine major crashes at a rate of 7.02 per 100,000 hours. The spike comes amid a separate, unresolved transmission problem affecting roughly 10% of the Army’s Apache fleet. Army safety messages identified 70 potentially faulty transmissions in April and another 10 in July. Failures can potentially affect the tail rotor, electrical power and hydraulics, creating the possibility of a sudden loss of control. The Army has not said how many of this year’s crashes are attributable to the transmission issue, and specifically cautions that its inclusion in safety reviews does not establish causation for any individual mishap. The root cause of the transmission failures remains under investigation, with Boeing assisting Army maintenance personnel. The latest fatal crash occurred Aug. 12 near Fort Hood, Texas, killing two pilots and prompting a temporary Army-wide pause in Apache training flights. That stand-down ended Wednesday, although deployed units in the Middle East were exempt.
